Competitive pressures and collective action problems together amplify AI risks by creating a situation where companies prioritize speed and capability over safety. Competitive pressures lead firms to reduce safety investments to maintain or improve their market position, resulting in a "race to the bottom" on safety. This dynamic encourages all companies to underinvest in safety measures, even when they recognize the collective benefits of such investments. 

Collective action problems further exacerbate this issue, as individual actors prefer to free-ride on the safety investments of others rather than bear the costs themselves. This leads to systematic underinvestment in safety across the industry, as companies face incentives to cut corners in safety testing and risk mitigation to keep up with competitors. The combination of these factors results in increased likelihood and severity of various AI risks, including misuse, misalignment, and systemic risks, as companies rush to deploy AI systems without adequate safety evaluations.
